The imported foundations are expressly granted by the task, so premises is empty. I independently opened the matching primary sources and checked their exact applications. For smooth existence, the base has dimension m≥2, α is strictly positive and closed, and (W/H)σ/L is smooth positive with total mass W. Closed Stokes forces the scaling constant in [Tosatti–Weinkove, Corollary 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0910.1390v2) to vanish. Multiplying the source potential by 2π gives the required dd^c convention. No endpoint equation or uniform endpoint PDE estimate is used.

A and n1 establish the full infimum. Expanding Ωε=Aε+Lw gives Ωε^n=(nW/H)μ and γε^m=L^−1Aε^m+mAε^(m−1)∧w. The first cofactor term is a base top-degree form; the second has closed factors. Thus γε is an actual smooth positive balanced test. Gauduchon Stokes and matrix AM–GM give the lower bound for every participating test, without a product restriction. The constructed metric attains it: its numerator is nW and its denominator is (nW/H)^(m/n)H. Consequently Vμ=nW/H.

The cost numerator is WJ/H, yielding C=n^−m/n W^(1/n)H^−(n+1)/n J. Since dH/ds=J, this equals −λ′. Holding any attaining test fixed gives λ(s+δ)≤λ(s)−δCξ for both signs of δ; differentiability of the explicit value forces Cξ=C. The strict negative-s extension handles s=0. No uniqueness, smooth metric family or measurable selection is assumed: every selection produces the same smooth scalar cost.

B's endpoint passage is valid. Let E be the raw endpoint infimum. Semipositivity gives E≥0, and α+w provides a finite test. Monotonicity gives lim λε≥E. For each fixed test, its quotient converges to its endpoint quotient, giving lim λε≤E after taking the infimum. The identical argument for θt+δh proves agreement with the specified Hermitian regularization for arbitrary h. Monotone convergence identifies H(0), including infinity, and therefore Vμ(θt)=nW/H(0). On every compact strict segment, the fundamental theorem gives ∫C=λ(0)−λ(r). The established endpoint limit and C≥0 then prove the finite improper identity. This covers all smooth a, including flat zeros, positive-measure zero sets and a≡0.

C and n2 justify all five geometric profiles. Positive density and bounded tubular Jacobians reduce the p-th inverse moment to 1+∫ρ^(d−1)/(ρ^k+ε)^p dρ. Substitution gives power divergence ε^(r−p) for r<p, logarithmic divergence for r=p, and a finite positive moment limit for r>p. Applying p=1,2 to the exact cost produces precisely the five claimed regimes. For r<1 the cost exponent exceeds −1; at r=1 the logarithmic denominator exponent exceeds one; for 1<r<2 the exponent r−2 exceeds −1. The logarithmic and bounded regimes are integrable too. The r>2 limit follows by domination. H(0)<∞ exactly when d>k. For finitely many disjoint components, positivity and finite summation make the smallest ratio govern both moments; no cancellation is possible.

D and n3 exclude every genuine strict potential. After comparing h with α+w, pair a purported strict current with fα^m for arbitrary smooth nonnegative base f. This is a smooth strongly semipositive, dd^c-closed test. Local integrability and distributional Stokes eliminate dd^c u, forcing a to have a positive uniform lower bound. A zero contradicts that conclusion. No current or singular potential is restricted to a fiber. Conversely, a positive minimum makes θt itself strictly positive.

The projective normalization also checks. With κ=dd^c log(1+|z|²), its affine volume density is (m!/π^m)(1+|z|²)^−(m+1)dLeb. Polar integration and x=|z|²/(1+|z|²) give the probability law mx^(m−1)dx, hence W=1. The unique zero has real codimension 2m and quadratic order. Thus H(0)=m/(m−1), Vμ(θt)=(m+1)(m−1)/m, and J(0)=m/(m−2) for m>2. The displayed m=2 formulas give logarithmic cost; for m>2 the stated positive finite limit follows. The polynomial-division recurrence in n3 is correct. These full-volume statements follow from A–B, rather than from a selected-test bound.

E and n4 have the exact closed comparison. The compact product is Kähler, P and Q are closed nef representatives, and their wedge expansions give ∫P^n=nW(a0+t) and ∫P^(n−1)Q=tW. Their Morse expression is nWa0, exactly Vμ(θt), independently of σ, including a0=0. [Tosatti, Theorem 1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.30153v2) applies precisely to compact Kähler manifolds and closed nef real cohomology classes, with the stated usual-volume convention. It supplies no comparison for nonclosed θt.

The universal core exclusion is valid under its hypothetical decomposition. [Demailly–Păun, Theorem 2.12](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0105176v2), together with the task-granted global potential consequence of the Kähler ddbar lemma, makes every proposed closed nef positive-intersection core strictly positive as a current after adding a genuine potential. Adding β and undoing the smooth gauge would make θt big, contradicting D. This covers arbitrary cores and gauges. The opposite gauge signs used in the article and n4 are equivalent by replacing f with −f. The smooth ddbar statement was also checked in [Demailly, VI.8.6–8.7](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~demarco/Math274/Demailly_ComplexAnalyticDiffGeom.pdf).

The ancillary calculations in n4 are correct: dθs=da∧w, dθs^m=m da∧α^(m−1)∧w, and dd^cθs^m=m dd^c a∧α^(m−1)∧w. Its gauge polynomial has derivative −nm∫(i/(2π))∂a∧bar∂a∧α^(m−1)<0 for nonconstant a, proving failure of ordinary top-integral gauge invariance. Its normalized density perturbation gives Hq=H+q(J−H²), with strictly positive variance for nonconstant a. Positivity and probability normalization hold for sufficiently small q.

Current companion overlap was checked directly. The repository's [warped section](https://github.com/MingchenXia/non-kahler-pluripotential-theory/blob/main/book/author/section_warped_gauduchon_completion.tex) already contains arbitrary-base product volume, balanced minimizers, tubular inverse-moment thresholds and the smooth-test nonbigness obstruction. Its [radial section](https://github.com/MingchenXia/non-kahler-pluripotential-theory/blob/main/book/author/section_radial_positive_volume_nonbig.tex) contains the scaled projective example. The [variational-volume chapter](https://github.com/MingchenXia/non-kahler-pluripotential-theory/blob/main/book/author/chapter_gauduchon_variational_volume.tex) already supplies first variation for any minimizer and nef-limit passage; the [closed-core section](https://github.com/MingchenXia/non-kahler-pluripotential-theory/blob/main/book/author/section_nef_boundary_subtraction.tex) contains its endpoint cost identity. These are credited background. The restricted cost profiles and reconstruction check mathematically, without establishing novelty or certifying the entire companion.

Harmless wording corrections: specify a∈C∞(B); state the nonempty-zero-set qualification for C, already explicit in n2, and handle an empty zero set by its positive minimum; write dθs not identically zero rather than suggesting pointwise nonvanishing. Replace the article's phrase that only W is gauge invariant: the Gauduchon quotient is also smoothly dd^c-gauge invariant, whereas ordinary nonclosed top integrals generally are not.
